clue.text: Such a moan may befit man lacking affection

definitions.text: Such a moan may befit man
definitions.meaning: read as an instruction: a moan with love, the tennis zero O, taken away is man, so it becomes fit to be man

explanation.surface: A lonely man without affection lets out a fitting groan.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic reading: remove 'love' (O, zero in tennis) from MOAN and MAN is left, so such a moan suits man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no love in it is without affection, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Jockey, 'onourable about payment, gets to meet with success

parts.note: Kieren Fallon was a champion flat-racing jockey

parts.note: honest, a word for honourable, with its H dropped as the apostrophe shows
a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: An honourable jockey who is paid comes good in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'onourable is a convention for a dropped H, as in Cockney speech; Kieren Fallon was a famous Irish jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: To land on your feet is an idiom for coming out of a situation well, succeeding by luck.
